title: Reduce hotpath request duplication and introduce priority/backpressure for console API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
The console backend is frequently creating duplicate work for high-concurrency dashboard requests. When many clients request overlapping slices (same user/project/time window) the request multiplexer fans out to multiple downstream resolvers and the aggregator rehydrates similar contexts repeatedly, leading to higher CPU, increased tail latency (P95 > 600ms on peak), and memory churn.

Goals:
- Eliminate duplicate upstream work for overlapping console queries by introducing in-process request coalescing and a small shared micro-batcher for short windows (<= 50ms).
- Add a priority queue and backpressure mechanism so interactive UI requests (user-hover / live updates) are prioritized over background polling and long-running analytics queries.
- Reduce per-request context duplication and GC pressure by reusing immutable payloads and moving large temporary buffers to a bounded pool.
- Upgrade the GraphQL server lib (graphql-js -> 17.x) to pick up resolver caching hooks and improved tracing; ensure compatibility with our custom field directives.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope includes console-api gateway, aggregator service, and GraphQL resolvers. Does NOT include: telemetry ingestion, unrelated microservices, or client SDK changes.

Proposed implementation summary:
1) Request coalescer: a small request-index keyed by (team_id, project_id, time_window_hash, route) that coalesces identical resolver hotpath requests within a 40ms debounce. New requests will await the in-flight promise instead of issuing a new downstream fetch. Implement in aggregator service (Go) with bounded slots to avoid unbounded queues.
2) Micro-batching: where resolvers touch the same backing read model, accumulate up to N requests in the 40ms window and issue a single batched DB/Key-value lookup.
3) Priority queue: add lightweight priority metadata to incoming HTTP headers from console gateway (X-Req-Priority: high|normal|low). Gateway will set priority for interactive routes. Aggregator will process high priority buckets first and will shed low-priority requests under sustained load.
4) Memory pool: refactor context construction to allocate large buffers from a sync.Pool (Go) and reuse immutable request envelopes across coalesced requests.
5) Dependency upgrade: bump graphql library to 17.x in console-api, run compatibility adapter for our directive handlers, and update types.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency on aggregated dashboard route reduced by >= 25% under a synthetic concurrency test that mirrors production (current baseline P95 640ms -> target <= 480ms).
- Overall CPU utilization on aggregator nodes decreased by >= 15% at peak within the test.
- No increase in error rate (5xx) during canary rollout.
- Unit and integration tests for coalescer and batching added; canary traffic shows coalescing hit rate >= 35% on target routes.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Feature flag off; deploy coalescer and priority logic behind flags to a small canary (10% traffic) with additional metric tags.
- Stage 2: Monitor for 6h (errors, p95, memory) then enable for 50% if stable.
- Stage 3: Full enable after 48h of stable metrics. Quick rollback switch to disable coalescing/prioritization is implemented in console-config.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: console/coalescer/hits, coalesce_latency_ms (histogram), priority_queue_depth, pool_allocations, resolver_batch_size.
- Alerts: coalescer_error_rate > 1% 5m, queue_depth > 200 for 2m, p95 degradation > 20% over baseline for 15m.

Dependencies & follow-ups:
- ENG-75321 (rework-request-multiplexer) - will coordinate to avoid overlapping mux changes.
- ENG-33012 (reduce-console-backend-noise) - this change should reduce noise but we must sync schema expectations.
- Follow-up ticket: collapse overlap windows into instrument-driven adaptive debounce (future).
